messages:
acme-infra: Hey team — since this morning we're getting truncated SSE streams from /v1/responses. The body arrives, but the final JSON object is cut (trailing '}' missing) and finish_reason is null. Happening ~10% of long-lived streams.

jess_support: Sorry to hear that — can you paste a minimal repro (curl) and an example of the truncated payload? Also any proxy/edge in front of you?

acme-infra: Repro below — we call with a long prompt and rotate our API key on TTL. Curl:```curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \ \  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \ \  https://api.redwood.example/v1/responses?stream=true```
Example stream we get (cut):```data: {"id":"resp_abc","choices":[{"delta":{"content":"..."}}, {"delta":{"content":"..."}}],"finish_reason":null}
data: {"id":"resp_abc","metadata":{"progress":100},"choices":[{"delta":{"content":"THE END"}}]``` — note final object truncated (ends mid-line) and client-side JSON parsing fails.

miguel_eng: Thanks, that helps. Two quick guesses: 1) an auth rotation happening mid-stream that triggers rejoin and the edge/proxy buffers/flushes partial frames, 2) keepalive pings (colon-prefixed SSE comments) getting treated weirdly and splitting the final event. Do you see any auth-refresh logs concurrent with requests?

acme-infra: Yes — our token refresh log shows a key swap at the same second as the stream end. We renew every 60s. Logs: "token-refresh: rotated key id=k-123 @1763004321" right when the request ended.

jess_support: That aligns with other cases. Can you try a short test: disable rotation for 2 minutes and replay the call, or set TTL to longer than the stream duration? Also share request_id from the failing call.

acme-infra: Request id: req-7f3b. We disabled rotation for a test and the same payload completed successfully once. So rotation looks correlated.

miguel_eng: Ok root cause likely proxy/ingress splitting the final chunk when the backend connection is reauthenticated/reused. On our side we should be emitting an explicit terminal SSE event (e.g., "data: [DONE]" or an explicit finish_reason field as a standalone event) and ensure it's flushed as its own packet. Short term: client workarounds:
- avoid rotating API key mid-stream (recommended)
- handle streaming by buffering until you see a terminal sentinel rather than depending on connection close
- accept and ignore SSE keepalive comments (lines starting with ":")

ops_ryan: Also check edge timeouts and buffering. If you're behind Fastly/NGINX/AWSALB, some configs will coalesce or truncate tail datagrams on backend connection swap. Increase idle_timeout to > 90s and disable proxy response buffering for that route.

acme-infra: Thanks — we'll try those. For production we can't stop rotation forever. Any server-side mitigations you can do?

miguel_eng: I'll open an internal ticket to emit a dedicated terminal event and to ensure the runtime flushes it. Patch idea (pseudo):```// at end-of-stream, send a separate SSE event so proxies don't fold it
data: {"id":"<id>","type":"terminal","finish_reason":"stop","final":true}

// then flush socket once, don't piggyback on previous frame```
I can push a canary to hosted API today and roll for Dedicated early next week.

deploy-bot: deploy notice: "canary/stream-terminal-event v0.3.1" rolled to 10% at 1763004440.

acme-infra: We tested against the canary endpoint with our normal rotation and the stream completed consistently in 8/8 runs. Great.

jess_support: Awesome — we'll keep this thread for follow-ups. Action items: Miguel to file INC-4521 and do a canary roll verification, Ops to publish recommended proxy config in docs, Acme to revert to normal rotation after verifications.

ops_ryan: I'll add nginx config snippet to the internal KB:```location /v1/responses {
  proxy_buffering off;
  proxy_read_timeout 120s;
  chunked_transfer_encoding on;
}```

miguel_eng: Filed INC-4521 and assigned to eng-runtime team. Will follow up with timeline and postmortem if needed.

acme-infra: Thanks everyone — removing our emergency alert. We'll reopen if we see other failures. :thumbsup:
